nodes.name: Neutral Tannakian duality
nodes.statement: The neutral Tannakian duality establishes a dictionary between $k$-linear tensor abelian categories, equipped with a fiber functor to the category of $k$-vector spaces, and affine group schemes over $k$.
nodes.statement_short: Tannakian duality matches $k$-linear tensor abelian categories with fiber functor and affine group schemes over $k$.
assumptions: Let $k$ be a field.
conclusions: The neutral Tannakian duality establishes a dictionary between $k$-linear tensor abelian categories, equipped with a fiber functor to the category of $k$-vector spaces, and affine group schemes over $k$.

nodes.name: The injectivity lemma (informal statement)
nodes.statement: The injectivity lemma claims that, under this correspondence, fully faithful exact functors, which preserves subobjects, correspond to injective homomorphisms of coalgebras (see Lemma \ref{lem2} for the precise formulation).
nodes.statement_short: Subobject-preserving fully faithful exact functors correspond exactly to injective coalgebra homomorphisms.
assumptions: Here, one first proves the claim for those categories which have a (pseudo-) generator. Such categories are in correspondence to finite dimensional coalgebras.
conclusions: fully faithful exact functors, which preserves subobjects, correspond to injective homomorphisms of coalgebras
nodes.origin_citation: Saavedra Rivano 2.6.3(f); Deligne & Milne Prop. 2.21; Szamuely Prop. 6.4.4; Hashimoto Lem. 3.6.10

nodes.name: Standing hypothesis: $R$ a commutative noetherian domain with quotient field $K$
nodes.statement: Throughout this work we shall fix a commutative noetherian domain $R$. The quotient field of $R$ will be denoted by $K$.

nodes.name: ${\rm mod}(A)$ and $\mod_{\rm f}(A)$
nodes.statement: For an algebra (or more general a ring) $A$ (commutative or not), ${\rm mod}(A)$ denotes the category of left $A$-modules and $\mod_{\rm f}(A)$ denotes the subcategory finitely generated modules.
differentia: $\mod_{\rm f}(A)$ denotes the subcategory finitely generated modules

nodes.name: ${\rm comod}(C)$ and $\comod_{\rm f}(C)$
nodes.statement: For a coalgebra $C$ over  $R$, ${\rm comod}(C)$ denotes the category of right $C$-comodules, and $\comod_{\rm f}(C)$ denotes the subcategory of comodules which are {\em finite over $R$}.
differentia: $\comod_{\rm f}(C)$ denotes the subcategory of comodules which are {\em finite over $R$}

nodes.name: The functor $\omega$ induced by a homomorphism of finite dimensional $k$-algebras is faithfully exact
nodes.statement: Let $k$ be a field and $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of finite dimensional $k$-algebras. Then $f$ induces a functor $\omega: \mod_{\rm f}(B)\to\mod_{\rm f}(A)$ between the categories of finite modules over $A$ and $B$, which is identity on the underlying vector spaces. In particular, $\omega$ is a faithfully exact functor.
nodes.statement_short: An algebra map $f:A\to B$ gives a restriction functor $\omega$ on finite modules that is the identity on underlying vector spaces, hence faithfully exact.
assumptions: Let $k$ be a field and $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of finite dimensional $k$-algebras.
conclusions: $f$ induces a functor $\omega: \mod_{\rm f}(B)\to\mod_{\rm f}(A)$ between the categories of finite modules over $A$ and $B$, which is identity on the underlying vector spaces
$\omega$ is a faithfully exact functor
nodes.section: 1 A simple proof of the injectivity lemma

nodes.name: Lemma 1.1 (surjectivity criterion for finite dimensional algebras)
nodes.statement: A homomorphism $f$ given as above is surjective if and only if the induced functor $\omega$ is full and has the property: for any $B$-module $X$ and any $A$-submodule $Y$ of $\omega(X)$, there exists a $B$-submodule $X'$ of $X$ such that $\omega(X')=Y$. In other words $f$ is surjective if and only if $\mod_{\rm f}(B)$, by means of $f$, is a full (abelian) subcategory of $\mod_{\rm f}(A)$, closed under taking submodules.
nodes.statement_short: $f$ is surjective iff $\mod_{\rm f}(B)$ sits in $\mod_{\rm f}(A)$ as a full subcategory closed under submodules.
assumptions: Let $k$ be a field and $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of finite dimensional $k$-algebras.
A homomorphism $f$ given as above
conclusions: A homomorphism $f$ given as above is surjective if and only if the induced functor $\omega$ is full and has the property: for any $B$-module $X$ and any $A$-submodule $Y$ of $\omega(X)$, there exists a $B$-submodule $X'$ of $X$ such that $\omega(X')=Y$.
In other words $f$ is surjective if and only if $\mod_{\rm f}(B)$, by means of $f$, is a full (abelian) subcategory of $\mod_{\rm f}(A)$, closed under taking submodules.
nodes.section: 1 A simple proof of the injectivity lemma

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1.1
nodes.statement: If $f$ is surjective then obviously $\omega$ has the claimed properties. We prove the converse statement. Thus for any $B$-module $X$ and any submodule $Y$ of $X$, considered as modules over $A$, we know that $Y$ is also stable under the action of $B$ (obtained by restricting the action of $B$ on $X$). Assume the contrary that $f$ is not surjective, i.e., $B_0:={\rm im} (f)$ is a strict subalgebra of $B$. Then $B_0\subset B$ is an inclusion of $A$-modules, $B$ it self is a $B$-module, but $B_0$ is not stable under the action of $B$ as it contains the unit of $B$. A contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: if $\rm{im}(f)$ were a strict subalgebra it would be an $A$-submodule of $B$ not stable under $B$, since it contains the unit.
nodes.section: 1 A simple proof of the injectivity lemma

nodes.name: Forward implication is immediate
nodes.statement: If $f$ is surjective then obviously $\omega$ has the claimed properties.
nodes.statement_short: Note the easy direction: surjectivity gives the functor properties.
nodes.section: 1 A simple proof of the injectivity lemma

nodes.name: Set up the converse: submodules are $B$-stable
nodes.statement: We prove the converse statement. Thus for any $B$-module $X$ and any submodule $Y$ of $X$, considered as modules over $A$, we know that $Y$ is also stable under the action of $B$ (obtained by restricting the action of $B$ on $X$).
nodes.statement_short: Restate the hypothesis as: every $A$-submodule of a $B$-module is $B$-stable.
nodes.section: 1 A simple proof of the injectivity lemma

nodes.name: Assume $f$ not surjective
nodes.statement: Assume the contrary that $f$ is not surjective, i.e., $B_0:={\rm im} (f)$ is a strict subalgebra of $B$.
nodes.statement_short: Suppose the image $B_0={\rm im}(f)$ is a strict subalgebra.
nodes.section: 1 A simple proof of the injectivity lemma

nodes.name: Contradiction via the unit of $B$
nodes.statement: Then $B_0\subset B$ is an inclusion of $A$-modules, $B$ it self is a $B$-module, but $B_0$ is not stable under the action of $B$ as it contains the unit of $B$. A contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Since $B_0$ contains the unit it cannot be $B$-stable, contradicting the hypothesis.
nodes.section: 1 A simple proof of the injectivity lemma

nodes.name: Lemma 1.2 (the injectivity lemma for finite dimensional coalgebras)
nodes.statement: Let $f:C\to D$ be a homomorphism of finite dimensional $k$-coalgebras. Then the category $\comod_{\rm f}(C)$, considered by means of $f$ as a subcategory of $\comod_{\rm f}(D)$, is full and closed under taking subobjects if and only if $f$ is injective.
nodes.statement_short: For finite dimensional coalgebras, $\comod_{\rm f}(C)\subset\comod_{\rm f}(D)$ is full and subobject-closed iff $f$ is injective.
assumptions: Let $f:C\to D$ be a homomorphism of finite dimensional $k$-coalgebras.
conclusions: the category $\comod_{\rm f}(C)$, considered by means of $f$ as a subcategory of $\comod_{\rm f}(D)$, is full and closed under taking subobjects if and only if $f$ is injective
nodes.section: 1 A simple proof of the injectivity lemma

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1.2 by duality
nodes.statement: By duality we have the following result for comodules.
nodes.statement_short: Dualize Lemma 1.1 from finite dimensional algebras to finite dimensional coalgebras.
nodes.section: 1 A simple proof of the injectivity lemma

nodes.name: Remark 1.3 (the dimension hypotheses can be dropped)
nodes.statement: In the proof of Lemma \ref{lem1}, there is no need to assume that $A$ is finite dimensional. Therefore, in Lemma \ref{lem2} there is no need to assume that $D$ is finite dimensional. On the other hand, it is known that each coalgebra is the union of its finite dimensional subcoalgebras. Therefore there is no need to impose the dimension condition on $C$ either.
nodes.statement_short: Neither $D$ nor $C$ needs to be finite dimensional in Lemma 1.2.

nodes.name: Every coalgebra is the union of its finite dimensional subcoalgebras
nodes.statement: On the other hand, it is known that each coalgebra is the union of its finite dimensional subcoalgebras.
conclusions: each coalgebra is the union of its finite dimensional subcoalgebras

nodes.name: $R$-finite (resp. torsion-free, flat, projective, free) module over an $R$-algebra
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a noetherian domain. We consider $R$-algebras. Modules over such an algebra are automatically $R$-modules, we call such a module $R$-finite (resp. torsion-free, flat, projective, free) if it is finite (resp. torsion-free, flat, projective, free) over $R$.
nodes.statement_short: A module over an $R$-algebra is called $R$-finite/torsion-free/flat/projective/free when it has that property over $R$.
differentia: it is finite (resp. torsion-free, flat, projective, free) over $R$

nodes.name: Base change subscript notation $( )_S$
nodes.statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative algebras. Then the base change $R\to S$ will be denoted by the subscript $( )_S$. For instance $M_S:=M\otimes_RS$, $f_S:=f\otimes_RS$ for an $R$-linear map $f$.

nodes.name: The functor $\omega$ induced by a homomorphism of finite torsion-free $R$-algebras is faithful and exact
nodes.statement: Let  $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of finite, torsion-free $R$-algebras. It induces a functor $\omega:\mod_\text{f}(B)\to \mod_\text{f}(A)$, which is identity functor on the underlying $R$-modules, therefore it is faithful and exact.
nodes.statement_short: Over a noetherian domain, restriction along $f$ is the identity on underlying $R$-modules, hence faithful and exact.
assumptions: Let  $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of finite, torsion-free $R$-algebras.
conclusions: It induces a functor $\omega:\mod_\text{f}(B)\to \mod_\text{f}(A)$, which is identity functor on the underlying $R$-modules
it is faithful and exact

nodes.name: Lemma 2.1 (surjectivity criterion over a noetherian domain)
nodes.statement: The map $f$ as above is surjective if and only if $\mod_{\rm f}(B)$ when considered by means of $f$ as a subcategory of $\mod_{\rm f}(A)$ is full and closed under taking subobjects.
nodes.statement_short: The surjectivity criterion of Lemma 1.1 holds for finite torsion-free algebras over a noetherian domain.
assumptions: Let  $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of finite, torsion-free $R$-algebras.
The map $f$ as above
conclusions: The map $f$ as above is surjective if and only if $\mod_{\rm f}(B)$ when considered by means of $f$ as a subcategory of $\mod_{\rm f}(A)$ is full and closed under taking subobjects.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: Only the ``if'' claim needs verification. Let $\mathfrak m\in R$ be a maximal ideal and let $k(\mathfrak m):=R/\mathfrak m$ be the residue field. Then the full subcategory of $\mod_{\rm f}(A)$ annihilated by $\mathfrak m$ is equivalent to $\mod_{\rm f}(A_{k(\mathfrak m)})$. Note that this subcategory is also closed under taking subobjects. Thus, by assumption, $\mod_{\rm f}(B_{k(\mathfrak m)})$ is a full subcategory of $\mod_{\rm f}(A_{k(\mathfrak m)})$, closed under taking subobjects. Therefore the map $f_{k(\mathfrak m)} :A_{k(\mathfrak m)}\to B_{k(\mathfrak m)}$ is surjective, by means of Lemma \ref{lem1}. This holds for any maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $R$, hence $(B/f(A))_{k(\mathfrak m)}=0$ for all maximal ideals $\mathfrak m$. According to \cite[Thm~4.8]{Mats}, we conclude that $B/f(A)$ itself is zero.
nodes.statement_short: Base change to every residue field $k(\mathfrak m)$, apply Lemma 1.1 fibrewise, then conclude $B/f(A)=0$ by a local-global vanishing result.

nodes.name: Reduce to the ``if'' direction
nodes.statement: Only the ``if'' claim needs verification.
nodes.statement_short: Only the sufficiency direction requires proof.

nodes.name: Pass to the residue field at a maximal ideal
nodes.statement: Let $\mathfrak m\in R$ be a maximal ideal and let $k(\mathfrak m):=R/\mathfrak m$ be the residue field. Then the full subcategory of $\mod_{\rm f}(A)$ annihilated by $\mathfrak m$ is equivalent to $\mod_{\rm f}(A_{k(\mathfrak m)})$. Note that this subcategory is also closed under taking subobjects.
nodes.statement_short: Identify the $\mathfrak m$-annihilated subcategory with modules over the fibre $A_{k(\mathfrak m)}$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 1.1 on each fibre
nodes.statement: Thus, by assumption, $\mod_{\rm f}(B_{k(\mathfrak m)})$ is a full subcategory of $\mod_{\rm f}(A_{k(\mathfrak m)})$, closed under taking subobjects. Therefore the map $f_{k(\mathfrak m)} :A_{k(\mathfrak m)}\to B_{k(\mathfrak m)}$ is surjective, by means of Lemma \ref{lem1}.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 1.1 gives surjectivity of $f_{k(\mathfrak m)}$ on every fibre.

nodes.name: Local vanishing implies global vanishing
nodes.statement: This holds for any maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $R$, hence $(B/f(A))_{k(\mathfrak m)}=0$ for all maximal ideals $\mathfrak m$. According to \cite[Thm~4.8]{Mats}, we conclude that $B/f(A)$ itself is zero.
nodes.statement_short: Vanishing at every maximal ideal forces $B/f(A)=0$.

nodes.name: Matsumura, Commutative ring theory, Thm 4.8
nodes.statement: hence $(B/f(A))_{k(\mathfrak m)}=0$ for all maximal ideals $\mathfrak m$. According to \cite[Thm~4.8]{Mats}, we conclude that $B/f(A)$ itself is zero.
nodes.statement_short: A finite module vanishing at every maximal ideal (after base change to the residue fields) is zero.
assumptions: $(B/f(A))_{k(\mathfrak m)}=0$ for all maximal ideals $\mathfrak m$
conclusions: $B/f(A)$ itself is zero

nodes.name: Remark on the choice of proof for Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: Lemma \ref{lem4} can also be proved in the same way as Lemma \ref{lem1}. We prefer to present the above proof as its main idea (using base change) will be exploited further.
nodes.statement_short: The base-change proof is presented because the technique recurs later.

nodes.name: Saturated submodule
nodes.statement: An $A$-submodule $N$ of $M$ is said to be {\em saturated} iff $M/N$ is $R$-torsion-free.

nodes.name: Dominant homomorphism
nodes.statement: A homomorphism $f:A\to B$ is said to be {\em dominant} if $f_K :A_K \to B_K$ is surjective, or equivalently $B/f(A)$ is $R$-torsion. Here $K$ denotes the quotient field of $R$.

nodes.name: Proposition 2.2 (dominance and surjectivity via saturated subobjects)
nodes.statement: Let $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of $R$-torsion free algebras and assume that $B$ is $R$-finite. Let $\omega:\mod_{\rm f}(B)\to\mod_{\rm f}(A)$ be the induced functor. Then: \begin{enumerate}\item The image of $\omega$ is closed under taking saturated subobjects of $R$-torsion-free objects iff $f$ is dominant. In this case $\omega$ is also closed under taking saturated submodules of any modules and its restriction to the subcategory of $R$-torsion-free modules is full. \item The image of $\omega$ is closed under taking subobjects of $R$-torsion-free objects iff $f$ is surjective. (In this case $\omega$ is also obviously full.) \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Closure of ${\rm im}(\omega)$ under saturated subobjects characterises dominance of $f$; closure under all subobjects of torsion-free objects characterises surjectivity.
assumptions: Let $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of $R$-torsion free algebras and assume that $B$ is $R$-finite.
Let $\omega:\mod_{\rm f}(B)\to\mod_{\rm f}(A)$ be the induced functor.
conclusions: The image of $\omega$ is closed under taking saturated subobjects of $R$-torsion-free objects iff $f$ is dominant. In this case $\omega$ is also closed under taking saturated submodules of any modules and its restriction to the subcategory of $R$-torsion-free modules is full.
The image of $\omega$ is closed under taking subobjects of $R$-torsion-free objects iff $f$ is surjective. (In this case $\omega$ is also obviously full.)

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.2
nodes.statement: (1). Assume that $\omega$ has the required property. We show that $f$ is dominant, i.e. $f_K$ is surjective. It suffices to show that the functor $\omega_K:\mod(B_K)\to \mod(A_K)$ induced from $f_K$ satisfies the condition of Lemma \ref{lem1}. Let $X$ be a finite $B_K$-module and $Y\subset X$ an $A_K$-submodule. Consider $X$ as a $B$-module, take a $K$-basis of $X$ such that a part of it is a basis of $Y$ and let $M$ be the $B$-submodule generated by this basis, let $N:=M\cap Y$. Then $N_K=Y$ (as it contains a $K$-basis of $Y$). By the diagram below $M/N$ is $R$-torsion-free. $$\xymatrix{0\ar[r]&N\ar[r]\ar@{^(->}[d]& M\ar[r]\ar@{^(->}[d]& M/N\ar[r]\ar@{^(->} [d]&0\\ 0\ar[r]& Y\ar[r]& X\ar[r]&X/Y\ar[r]&0.}$$ Thus $N$ is a saturated submodule of $M$, hence, by assumption, $N$ is stable under $B$, consequently $Y=N_K$ is stable under $B_K$. Conversely, assume that $f$ is dominant, i.e., $f_K$ is surjective. Then $\omega_K$ is fully faithful and closed under taking submodules. Let $M$ be an $R$-torsion-free $B$-module, $N\subset M$ be a saturated $A$-submodule. Then $M/N$ is also $R$-torsion-free, hence $N=M\cap N_K$. Now $N_K$ is stable under $B_K$ and $M$ is stable under $B$, showing that $N$ is stable under $B$. Let $\varphi:M\to N$ be an $A$-linear map, where $M,N$ are both $R$-torsion-free then $\varphi$ is determined by $\varphi_K:M_K\to N_K$. Since $f_K$ is surjective, we know that $\varphi_K$ is $A_K$-linear, hence also $B_K$-linear, implying that $f$ is $B$-linear. Thus $\omega$ restricted to $R$-torsion free modules is full. Let now $M$ be a finite $A$-module, $N$ be a finite $B$-module and $\varphi:M\to N$ be an injective $A$-linear map with $M/\varphi(N)$ being $R$-torsion free. Consider a finite free $B$-linear cover $\psi:N'\to N$. Let $\varphi':M'\to N'$ be the pull-back of $\varphi$ along $\psi$ (as $A$-modules). $$\xymatrix{M'\ar@{->>}[d]_{\psi'}\ar@{^(->}[r]^{\varphi'}&N'\ar@{->>}[d]^\psi\\ M\ar@{^(->}[r]_\varphi &N.}$$ Then $\varphi'$ is injective and $\psi':M'\to M$ is surjective, moreover $N'/\varphi'(M')\cong N/\varphi(N)$ hence is $R$-torsion free. Consequently, $M'$ is $B$-stable and, since $\varphi\psi'=\psi\varphi'$ is $B$-linear, there is a $B$-action on $M$ making $\varphi$ $B$-linear. (2). According to the proof of Lemma \ref{lem4}, it suffices to show that for any maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $R$, the image of $\omega_{k(\mathfrak m)}$ is closed under taking submodules. Let $V$ be a $B_{k(\mathfrak m)}$-module and let $\varphi:U\to V$ be an inclusion of $A_{k(\mathfrak m)}$-modules. Represent $V$ as a quotient of some (free) $B$-modules $M$, then $U$ will be a quotient of some $A$-submodule $N$ of $M$. We have $N$ is $R$-torsion-free, hence, by assumption, $N$ is stable under $B$,  so that $U$ must be $B_{k(\mathfrak m)}$-stable.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the generic fibre and apply Lemma 1.1 for (1); for (2) base change to each residue field as in the proof of Lemma 2.1.

nodes.name: Part (1): reduce dominance to the condition of Lemma 1.1 over $K$
nodes.statement: (1). Assume that $\omega$ has the required property. We show that $f$ is dominant, i.e. $f_K$ is surjective. It suffices to show that the functor $\omega_K:\mod(B_K)\to \mod(A_K)$ induced from $f_K$ satisfies the condition of Lemma \ref{lem1}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce dominance of $f$ to verifying Lemma 1.1's hypothesis for $\omega_K$.

nodes.name: Construct a saturated integral model $N\subset M$ of $Y\subset X$
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a finite $B_K$-module and $Y\subset X$ an $A_K$-submodule. Consider $X$ as a $B$-module, take a $K$-basis of $X$ such that a part of it is a basis of $Y$ and let $M$ be the $B$-submodule generated by this basis, let $N:=M\cap Y$. Then $N_K=Y$ (as it contains a $K$-basis of $Y$). By the diagram below $M/N$ is $R$-torsion-free. $$\xymatrix{0\ar[r]&N\ar[r]\ar@{^(->}[d]& M\ar[r]\ar@{^(->}[d]& M/N\ar[r]\ar@{^(->} [d]&0\\ 0\ar[r]& Y\ar[r]& X\ar[r]&X/Y\ar[r]&0.}$$ Thus $N$ is a saturated submodule of $M$, hence, by assumption, $N$ is stable under $B$, consequently $Y=N_K$ is stable under $B_K$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose an adapted $K$-basis to build a saturated $R$-lattice, so $B$-stability descends and then extends to $B_K$.

nodes.name: Converse: dominance implies saturated submodules are $B$-stable
nodes.statement: Conversely, assume that $f$ is dominant, i.e., $f_K$ is surjective. Then $\omega_K$ is fully faithful and closed under taking submodules. Let $M$ be an $R$-torsion-free $B$-module, $N\subset M$ be a saturated $A$-submodule. Then $M/N$ is also $R$-torsion-free, hence $N=M\cap N_K$. Now $N_K$ is stable under $B_K$ and $M$ is stable under $B$, showing that $N$ is stable under $B$.
nodes.statement_short: From surjectivity of $f_K$, recover $N=M\cap N_K$ and deduce $B$-stability of $N$.

nodes.name: Fullness on $R$-torsion-free modules
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi:M\to N$ be an $A$-linear map, where $M,N$ are both $R$-torsion-free then $\varphi$ is determined by $\varphi_K:M_K\to N_K$. Since $f_K$ is surjective, we know that $\varphi_K$ is $A_K$-linear, hence also $B_K$-linear, implying that $f$ is $B$-linear. Thus $\omega$ restricted to $R$-torsion free modules is full.
nodes.statement_short: An $A$-linear map of torsion-free modules is determined generically, hence is $B$-linear.

nodes.name: Free cover and pull-back to transport the $B$-action
nodes.statement: Let now $M$ be a finite $A$-module, $N$ be a finite $B$-module and $\varphi:M\to N$ be an injective $A$-linear map with $M/\varphi(N)$ being $R$-torsion free. Consider a finite free $B$-linear cover $\psi:N'\to N$. Let $\varphi':M'\to N'$ be the pull-back of $\varphi$ along $\psi$ (as $A$-modules). $$\xymatrix{M'\ar@{->>}[d]_{\psi'}\ar@{^(->}[r]^{\varphi'}&N'\ar@{->>}[d]^\psi\\ M\ar@{^(->}[r]_\varphi &N.}$$ Then $\varphi'$ is injective and $\psi':M'\to M$ is surjective, moreover $N'/\varphi'(M')\cong N/\varphi(N)$ hence is $R$-torsion free. Consequently, $M'$ is $B$-stable and, since $\varphi\psi'=\psi\varphi'$ is $B$-linear, there is a $B$-action on $M$ making $\varphi$ $B$-linear.
nodes.statement_short: Pull back along a finite free $B$-cover to descend a $B$-action to $M$.

nodes.name: Part (2): reduce to the residue fibres as in Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: (2). According to the proof of Lemma \ref{lem4}, it suffices to show that for any maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $R$, the image of $\omega_{k(\mathfrak m)}$ is closed under taking submodules. Let $V$ be a $B_{k(\mathfrak m)}$-module and let $\varphi:U\to V$ be an inclusion of $A_{k(\mathfrak m)}$-modules. Represent $V$ as a quotient of some (free) $B$-modules $M$, then $U$ will be a quotient of some $A$-submodule $N$ of $M$. We have $N$ is $R$-torsion-free, hence, by assumption, $N$ is stable under $B$,  so that $U$ must be $B_{k(\mathfrak m)}$-stable.
nodes.statement_short: Lift a fibrewise inclusion to torsion-free modules over $R$ and use the hypothesis there.

nodes.name: Comodule categories over $R$-flat coalgebras are abelian
nodes.statement: For such coalgebras the comodule categories are abelian, see, e.g. \cite[Lem.~3.3.3]{Ha} or \cite[Thm.~3.13]{BW}. Moreover, the kernel and image of a comodule  homomorphism are the same as those of the underlying $R$-module homomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: For flat coalgebras $\comod(C)$ is abelian and kernels/images are computed on underlying $R$-modules.
assumptions: In this subsection we consider $R$-flat coalgebras.
conclusions: the comodule categories are abelian
the kernel and image of a comodule  homomorphism are the same as those of the underlying $R$-module homomorphism

nodes.name: The restriction functor $\omega:\comod(C)\to\comod(D)$ is faithful and exact
nodes.statement: A homomorphism of flat $R$-coalgebras $f:C\to D$ induces the restriction functor $\omega:\comod(C)\to \comod(D)$ which is the identity functor on the underlying $R$-module. Hence $\omega$ is faithful and exact.
nodes.statement_short: Restriction along a flat coalgebra map is the identity on underlying $R$-modules, hence faithful and exact.
assumptions: A homomorphism of flat $R$-coalgebras $f:C\to D$
conclusions: induces the restriction functor $\omega:\comod(C)\to \comod(D)$ which is the identity functor on the underlying $R$-module
$\omega$ is faithful and exact

nodes.name: Pure homomorphism of flat $R$-coalgebras
nodes.statement: We say that a homomorphism of flat $R$-coalgebras $f:C\to D$ is pure if it is  a pure homomorphism of $R$-modules. This condition is the same as requiring $D/f(C)$ be $R$-flat.
differentia: it is  a pure homomorphism of $R$-modules

nodes.name: Finite flat modules over a noetherian domain are projective
nodes.statement: Note also that over a noetherian domain, finite flat modules are projective.
assumptions: over a noetherian domain
conclusions: finite flat modules are projective
nodes.origin_citation: standard commutative algebra fact; stated without citation

nodes.name: Lemma 2.3 (dualization: injectivity vs. dominance of $f^\vee$)
nodes.statement: Let $C$ be an $R$-finite flat (hence projective) module and $D$ be an $R$-projective module. Then: \begin{enumerate}\item $f$ is injective iff $f^\vee:D^\vee\to C^\vee$ is dominant; \item $f$ is injective and pure iff $f^\vee:D^\vee\to C^\vee$ is surjective, \end{enumerate} where $C^\vee:={\rm Hom}_R(C,R)$.
nodes.statement_short: Injectivity of $f$ dualizes to dominance of $f^\vee$, and injectivity plus purity to surjectivity of $f^\vee$.
assumptions: Let $C$ be an $R$-finite flat (hence projective) module and $D$ be an $R$-projective module.
A homomorphism of flat $R$-coalgebras $f:C\to D$
conclusions: $f$ is injective iff $f^\vee:D^\vee\to C^\vee$ is dominant
$f$ is injective and pure iff $f^\vee:D^\vee\to C^\vee$ is surjective

nodes.name: $R$-dual $C^\vee$
nodes.statement: where $C^\vee:={\rm Hom}_R(C,R)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.3
nodes.statement: Embedding $D$ as a direct summand into a free module does not change the properties of $f$ and $f^\vee$, hence we can assume that $D$ is free. Since $C$ is finite, there exists a finite direct summand of $D$ which contains the image of $f$ and we can replace $D$ by this summand, that means we can assume that $D$ is finite. The claims for finite projective modules are obvious. For (1), it involves only the generic fibers. For (2), $f:C\to D$ is pure iff $D/f(C)$ projective, and iff the sequence $0\to C\to D\to D/f(C)\to 0$ is split exact, iff the sequence $0\to (D/f(C))^\vee\to D^\vee\to C^\vee\to 0$ is split exact.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to finite free $D$ by direct-summand arguments, then read off both claims from split exactness of the dual sequence.

nodes.name: Reduce to $D$ free
nodes.statement: Embedding $D$ as a direct summand into a free module does not change the properties of $f$ and $f^\vee$, hence we can assume that $D$ is free.
nodes.statement_short: Assume $D$ free, using that direct summands preserve the properties in question.

nodes.name: Reduce to $D$ finite
nodes.statement: Since $C$ is finite, there exists a finite direct summand of $D$ which contains the image of $f$ and we can replace $D$ by this summand, that means we can assume that $D$ is finite.
nodes.statement_short: Replace $D$ by a finite summand containing ${\rm im}(f)$, so $D$ may be assumed finite.

nodes.name: Part (1) via the generic fibre
nodes.statement: The claims for finite projective modules are obvious. For (1), it involves only the generic fibers.
nodes.statement_short: For finite projective modules claim (1) is a generic-fibre statement.

nodes.name: Part (2) via split exactness of the dual sequence
nodes.statement: For (2), $f:C\to D$ is pure iff $D/f(C)$ projective, and iff the sequence $0\to C\to D\to D/f(C)\to 0$ is split exact, iff the sequence $0\to (D/f(C))^\vee\to D^\vee\to C^\vee\to 0$ is split exact.
nodes.statement_short: Chain the equivalences purity $\Leftrightarrow$ projectivity of the cokernel $\Leftrightarrow$ split exactness before and after dualizing.

nodes.name: Saturated subcomodule
nodes.statement: A subcomodule $N$ of a $C$-comodule $M$ said to be saturated if $M/N$ is $R$-torsion free.

nodes.name: Proposition 2.4 (injectivity criterion for $R$-projective coalgebras)
nodes.statement: Let $C,D$ be $R$-projective coalgebras. Let $f:C\to D$ be a homomorphism of $R$-coalgebras and $\omega:\comod_{\rm f}(C)\to\comod_{\rm f}(D)$ be the induced functor. Assume that $C$ is $R$-finite. Then: \begin{enumerate} \item The image of functor $\omega$ is closed under taking saturated subcomodules of $R$- torsion-free comodules iff $f$ is injective. In this case $\omega$ is also closed under taking saturated subcomodules of any comodules and its restriction to the subcategory of $R$-torsion-free comodules is full. \item The image of functor $\omega$ is closed under taking subcomodules of $R$-torsion-free comodules iff $f$ is injective and pure. (In this case $\omega$ is also obviously full.) \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: For $R$-projective coalgebras with $C$ finite: saturated-subcomodule closure characterises injectivity, full subcomodule closure characterises injectivity plus purity.
assumptions: Let $C,D$ be $R$-projective coalgebras.
Let $f:C\to D$ be a homomorphism of $R$-coalgebras and $\omega:\comod_{\rm f}(C)\to\comod_{\rm f}(D)$ be the induced functor.
Assume that $C$ is $R$-finite.
conclusions: The image of functor $\omega$ is closed under taking saturated subcomodules of $R$- torsion-free comodules iff $f$ is injective. In this case $\omega$ is also closed under taking saturated subcomodules of any comodules and its restriction to the subcategory of $R$-torsion-free comodules is full.
The image of functor $\omega$ is closed under taking subcomodules of $R$-torsion-free comodules iff $f$ is injective and pure. (In this case $\omega$ is also obviously full.)

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.4
nodes.statement: Since $D$ is projective, the natural functor ${\rm comod}(D)\to \mod(D^\vee)$ is fully faithful, exact with image closed under taking subobjects \cite[3.10]{Ha}. Thus the functor, induced from $\omega$, $\mod(D^\vee)\to \mod(C^\vee)$ is fully faithful, exact and has image closed under taking subobjects iff $\omega$ is. The claim follows from Proposition \ref{prop5} and Lemma \ref{lem6}.
nodes.statement_short: Transfer the statement across the fully faithful embedding $\comod(D)\hookrightarrow\mod(D^\vee)$ and apply Proposition 2.2 with Lemma 2.3.

nodes.name: Embed $\comod(D)$ into $\mod(D^\vee)$
nodes.statement: Since $D$ is projective, the natural functor ${\rm comod}(D)\to \mod(D^\vee)$ is fully faithful, exact with image closed under taking subobjects \cite[3.10]{Ha}.
nodes.statement_short: Invoke the fully faithful exact embedding of comodules into $D^\vee$-modules.

nodes.name: Transfer the properties to the dual module categories
nodes.statement: Thus the functor, induced from $\omega$, $\mod(D^\vee)\to \mod(C^\vee)$ is fully faithful, exact and has image closed under taking subobjects iff $\omega$ is.
nodes.statement_short: The required properties for $\omega$ are equivalent to those for the induced map of dual module categories.

nodes.name: Conclude from Proposition 2.2 and Lemma 2.3
nodes.statement: The claim follows from Proposition \ref{prop5} and Lemma \ref{lem6}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the algebra-side proposition with the dualization lemma.

nodes.name: Locally finite flat $R$-coalgebra (IFP)
nodes.statement: We say that a flat $R$-coalgebra $C$ is locally finite if $C$ is the union of its finite $R$-projective pure subcoalgebras $C_\alpha$, $\alpha\in A$. This property is called IFP (ind-finite projective property) in \cite{Ha}.
differentia: $C$ is the union of its finite $R$-projective pure subcoalgebras $C_\alpha$, $\alpha\in A$

nodes.name: Corollary 2.5 (injectivity criterion for coalgebras with IFP)
nodes.statement: Let $C,D$ be projective $R$-coalgebras. Assume that $C$ has IFP, $C=\bigcup C_\alpha$. Let $f:C\to D$ be a homomorphism of $R$-coalgebras. Then $f$ is injective iff the induced functor $\omega:\comod_{\rm f}(C)\to\comod_f(D)$ has image closed under taking subobjects. In particular, $\comod_{\rm f}(C)$ is the union of its full subcategories $\comod_{\rm f}(C_\alpha)$, which are closed under taking subobjects.
nodes.statement_short: If $C$ has IFP, injectivity of $f$ is equivalent to subobject-closure of ${\rm im}(\omega)$, without any finiteness assumption on $C$.
assumptions: Let $C,D$ be projective $R$-coalgebras.
Assume that $C$ has IFP, $C=\bigcup C_\alpha$.
Let $f:C\to D$ be a homomorphism of $R$-coalgebras.
conclusions: $f$ is injective iff the induced functor $\omega:\comod_{\rm f}(C)\to\comod_f(D)$ has image closed under taking subobjects
In particular, $\comod_{\rm f}(C)$ is the union of its full subcategories $\comod_{\rm f}(C_\alpha)$, which are closed under taking subobjects.

nodes.name: Existence of $R$-flat coalgebras with almost no finite pure subcoalgebras
nodes.statement: Notice that there exist $R$-flat coalgebras which contains almost no finite pure subcoalgebras, as shown in the examples below.
conclusions: there exist $R$-flat coalgebras which contains almost no finite pure subcoalgebras

nodes.name: Example 2.6(1) ($H=R[T]/(\pi T^2+T)$ in characteristic 2)
nodes.statement: (1) Assume that $R$ is a Dedekind ring with characteristic equal to 2 and $\pi\neq 0$ is a non-unit in $R$. Consider the algebra $H:=R[T]/(\pi T^2+T)$ with the coalgebra structure given by $$\Delta(T)=T\otimes 1+1\otimes T.$$ Then $H$ is torsion-free, hence flat over $R$. Let $M\subset H$ be a saturated $R$-finite subcomodule of $H$. Then $M$ is free over $R$, more over its rank is at most 2, as $H_K$ has dimension 2 over $K$. If $M$ has rank 2 then $H/M$ is $R$-torsion, contradiction, hence $M$ has rank 1 over $R$. The coaction of $H$ on $M$ is thus given by a group-like element in $H$. On the other hand, the $R$-flatness of $H$ implies $H\otimes H$ is a submodule of $H_K\otimes_KH_K$, hence the coproduct on $H$ is the restriction of the coproduct on $H_K$: $$\xymatrix{H\ar[r]^{\Delta\quad}\ar[d]& H\otimes H\ar[d]\\ H_K\ar[r]_{\Delta\qquad}& H_K\otimes_KH_K.}$$ Consequently, a group-like element of $H$ is a group-like element of $H_K$. But in $H_K$ the unique group-like element is 1. Thus $M$ is a trivial comodule of $H$.
nodes.statement_short: A flat Hopf-like coalgebra $R[T]/(\pi T^2+T)$ in characteristic 2 whose only saturated finite subcomodules are trivial.
nodes.origin_citation: J. P. dos Santos, private communication

nodes.name: Example 2.6(2) ($H=R[T]/(\pi T^2+2T)$ with 2 invertible)
nodes.statement: (2) Similarly, assume that $R$ is a Dedekind ring, in which 2 is invertible. Consider the algebra $H:=R[T]/(\pi T^2+2T)$ where $\pi\neq 0$ is a non-unit. $H$ is a Hopf algebra with the coaction given by $$\Delta(T)=T\otimes 1+1\otimes T+\pi T\otimes T.$$ Similar discussion shows that there are only two finite saturated subcomodules of $H$, the one generated by 1 and the other generated by the group-like element $1+\pi T$.
nodes.statement_short: The Hopf algebra $R[T]/(\pi T^2+2T)$ has only two finite saturated subcomodules, generated by $1$ and by $1+\pi T$.
nodes.origin_citation: J. P. dos Santos, private communication

nodes.name: Strategy for general coalgebra homomorphisms
nodes.statement: To treat a general coalgebra homomorphism $f:C\to D$ we shall imitate the proof of Lemma \ref{lem1}. Our condition on $\omega$ will be some what stronger.
nodes.statement_short: The general case imitates the proof of Lemma 1.1 under a slightly stronger hypothesis on $\omega$.

nodes.name: Proposition 2.7 (injectivity criterion for $R$-flat coalgebras)
nodes.statement: Let $C,D$ be $R$-flat coalgebras  and  $f:C\to D$ be a homomorphism of $R$-coalgebras. Let $\omega:\comod(C)\to\comod(D)$ be the induced functor on comodule categories. Then: \begin{enumerate} \item The image of functor $\omega$ is closed under taking saturated subcomodules of $R$-torsion-free comodules iff $f$ is injective. In this case $\omega$ is also closed under taking saturated subcomodules of any comodules and its restriction to the subcategory of $R$-torsion-free comodules is full. \item The image of functor $\omega$ is closed under taking subcomodules of any comodules iff $f$ is injective and pure. In this case $\omega$ is full. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: For arbitrary $R$-flat coalgebras: saturated-subcomodule closure characterises injectivity of $f$, and closure under all subcomodules characterises injectivity plus purity.
assumptions: Let $C,D$ be $R$-flat coalgebras  and  $f:C\to D$ be a homomorphism of $R$-coalgebras.
Let $\omega:\comod(C)\to\comod(D)$ be the induced functor on comodule categories.
conclusions: The image of functor $\omega$ is closed under taking saturated subcomodules of $R$-torsion-free comodules iff $f$ is injective. In this case $\omega$ is also closed under taking saturated subcomodules of any comodules and its restriction to the subcategory of $R$-torsion-free comodules is full.
The image of functor $\omega$ is closed under taking subcomodules of any comodules iff $f$ is injective and pure. In this case $\omega$ is full.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.7
nodes.statement: (1) Assume that $\omega$ has the required property. Let $C_0:={\rm ker}(f)$. Then $C/C_0\cong {\rm im}(f)\subset D$ is $R$-torsion-free, hence $C_0$ is a saturated subcomodule of $C$, considered as $D$-comodules (the big left square with curved vertical arrows below is commutative). By assumption, the coaction of $D$ on $C_0$ lifts to a coaction of $C$. That is, there exists a coaction $C_0\to C_0\otimes C$ (the dotted arrow below) making the following diagram commutative: $$\xymatrix{ C_0\ar[r] \ar@{-->}[d]\ar@/_30pt/[dd] &C\ar[d]^\Delta\ar[r]^f\ar@/^30pt/[dd] & D\ar[dd]^\Delta \\ C_0\otimes C\ar[r]\ar[d]^{{\rm id}\otimes f}& C\otimes C\ar[d]^{{\rm id}\otimes f}&\\ C_0\otimes D\ar[r]&C\otimes D\ar[r]_{f\otimes {\rm id}}&D\otimes D.}$$ In particular, the coaction of $C$ on $C_0$ is the restriction of that on $C$ (the upper-left square). That is, for any $c\in C_0$ we have a representation $$\Delta(c)=\sum_{(c)}c_{(1)}\otimes c_{(2)},$$ with $c_{(1)}\in C_0$. On the other hand, as $f$ is a coalgebra homomorphism, we have $\varepsilon\circ f=\varepsilon$. Consequently, $\varepsilon(C_0)=0$. Applying $\varepsilon\otimes{\rm id}$ to the above equation we get $$c=\sum_{(c)}\varepsilon(c_{(1)})\otimes c_{(2)}=0.$$ A contradiction. Thus ${\rm ker}(f)=0$. Conversely, assume that $f:C\to D$ is injective, then the map $f_K:C_K\to D_K$ is also injective, as the base change $R\to K$ is flat. Hence, according to \ref{lem2}, \ref{rmk3}, $\omega_K$ is fully faithful and is closed under taking subcomodules. Thus $\omega$ is full when restricted to $R$-torsion free comodules. Finally we show that the image of $\omega$ is closed under taking saturated subcomodules of any comodules. For an $R$-module $M$, let $M^\text{tor}$ denote its torsion part, i.e. those elements of $M$ killed by some non-zero element of $R$. Then we have $$M^\text{tor}={\rm ker}(M\to M\otimes K).$$ Therefore, for any flat $R$-module $P$ we have $$(M^\text{tor}\otimes P)\cong (M\otimes P)^\text{tor}.$$ Since any $R$-linear map preserves the torsion part, we conclude that, if $M$ is a $C$-comodule then $M^\text{tor}$ is a subcomodule. Let now $N\subset M$ be a subcomodule with respect to the action of $D$. If $M/N$ is $R$-torsion free then $M^\text{tor}=N^\text{tor}$ and hence is stable under the coaction of $C$. Hence we can consider the saturated inclusion $N/N^\text{tor}\subset M/M^\text{tor}$, which by assumption shows that $N/N^\text{tor}$ is stable under the coaction of $C$. As $C$ is flat, we conclude that $N$ itself is stable under $C$. (2) Assume that $\omega$ is closed under taking subcomodules of any comodules. Then according to (1), $f$ is injective. Assume $f$ is not pure, then there exists an ideal $I$ of $R$ such that the induced map $R/I\otimes C\to R/I\otimes D$ is not injective. Let $C_0$ be the kernel of this map. Repeat the argument of the proof of (1) we conclude that $C_0$ is stable under the coaction of $D$ but not under the coaction of $C$, a contradiction. Thus $f$ has to be pure. For the converse, assuming that $f:C\to D$ is injective and pure and $N\subset M$ be $R$-modules, then we have the equality of submodules of $M\otimes D$: $$N\otimes D\cap M\otimes C=N\otimes C,$$ where $C$ is considered as an $R$-submodule of $D$ by means of $f$. Hence, if $M$ is a $C$-comodule and $N$ is a $D$-subcomodule of $M$, then, denote by $\delta$ the coaction, we have $$\delta(N)\subset N\otimes D\cap M\otimes C=N\otimes C.$$ That is, $N$ is stable under the coaction of $C$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the counit to a lifted coaction on $C_0={\rm ker}(f)$ to force $C_0=0$; then use flat base change, torsion-part identities and the purity intersection identity for the remaining claims.

nodes.name: Part (1): $C_0={\rm ker}(f)$ is a saturated subcomodule
nodes.statement: (1) Assume that $\omega$ has the required property. Let $C_0:={\rm ker}(f)$. Then $C/C_0\cong {\rm im}(f)\subset D$ is $R$-torsion-free, hence $C_0$ is a saturated subcomodule of $C$, considered as $D$-comodules (the big left square with curved vertical arrows below is commutative).
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the kernel $C_0$ and observe it is saturated as a $D$-subcomodule.

nodes.name: Lift the $D$-coaction on $C_0$ to a $C$-coaction
nodes.statement: By assumption, the coaction of $D$ on $C_0$ lifts to a coaction of $C$. That is, there exists a coaction $C_0\to C_0\otimes C$ (the dotted arrow below) making the following diagram commutative: $$\xymatrix{ C_0\ar[r] \ar@{-->}[d]\ar@/_30pt/[dd] &C\ar[d]^\Delta\ar[r]^f\ar@/^30pt/[dd] & D\ar[dd]^\Delta \\ C_0\otimes C\ar[r]\ar[d]^{{\rm id}\otimes f}& C\otimes C\ar[d]^{{\rm id}\otimes f}&\\ C_0\otimes D\ar[r]&C\otimes D\ar[r]_{f\otimes {\rm id}}&D\otimes D.}$$
nodes.statement_short: Use the hypothesis to obtain a $C$-coaction $C_0\to C_0\otimes C$ compatible with $\Delta$.

nodes.name: Apply the counit to get $C_0=0$
nodes.statement: In particular, the coaction of $C$ on $C_0$ is the restriction of that on $C$ (the upper-left square). That is, for any $c\in C_0$ we have a representation $$\Delta(c)=\sum_{(c)}c_{(1)}\otimes c_{(2)},$$ with $c_{(1)}\in C_0$. On the other hand, as $f$ is a coalgebra homomorphism, we have $\varepsilon\circ f=\varepsilon$. Consequently, $\varepsilon(C_0)=0$. Applying $\varepsilon\otimes{\rm id}$ to the above equation we get $$c=\sum_{(c)}\varepsilon(c_{(1)})\otimes c_{(2)}=0.$$ A contradiction. Thus ${\rm ker}(f)=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Applying $\varepsilon\otimes{\rm id}$ to $\Delta(c)$ gives $c=0$, so ${\rm ker}(f)=0$.

nodes.name: Converse: pass to the generic fibre and apply Lemma 1.2 with Remark 1.3
nodes.statement: Conversely, assume that $f:C\to D$ is injective, then the map $f_K:C_K\to D_K$ is also injective, as the base change $R\to K$ is flat. Hence, according to \ref{lem2}, \ref{rmk3}, $\omega_K$ is fully faithful and is closed under taking subcomodules. Thus $\omega$ is full when restricted to $R$-torsion free comodules.
nodes.statement_short: Injectivity survives flat base change to $K$, so Lemma 1.2 applies to $\omega_K$.

nodes.name: Extend saturated-subcomodule closure to arbitrary comodules via torsion parts
nodes.statement: Finally we show that the image of $\omega$ is closed under taking saturated subcomodules of any comodules. For an $R$-module $M$, let $M^\text{tor}$ denote its torsion part, i.e. those elements of $M$ killed by some non-zero element of $R$. Then we have $$M^\text{tor}={\rm ker}(M\to M\otimes K).$$ Therefore, for any flat $R$-module $P$ we have $$(M^\text{tor}\otimes P)\cong (M\otimes P)^\text{tor}.$$ Since any $R$-linear map preserves the torsion part, we conclude that, if $M$ is a $C$-comodule then $M^\text{tor}$ is a subcomodule. Let now $N\subset M$ be a subcomodule with respect to the action of $D$. If $M/N$ is $R$-torsion free then $M^\text{tor}=N^\text{tor}$ and hence is stable under the coaction of $C$. Hence we can consider the saturated inclusion $N/N^\text{tor}\subset M/M^\text{tor}$, which by assumption shows that $N/N^\text{tor}$ is stable under the coaction of $C$. As $C$ is flat, we conclude that $N$ itself is stable under $C$.
nodes.statement_short: Split off torsion parts, apply the torsion-free case to $N/N^{\rm tor}\subset M/M^{\rm tor}$, and use flatness of $C$ to descend.

nodes.name: Part (2): failure of purity yields a contradiction
nodes.statement: (2) Assume that $\omega$ is closed under taking subcomodules of any comodules. Then according to (1), $f$ is injective. Assume $f$ is not pure, then there exists an ideal $I$ of $R$ such that the induced map $R/I\otimes C\to R/I\otimes D$ is not injective. Let $C_0$ be the kernel of this map. Repeat the argument of the proof of (1) we conclude that $C_0$ is stable under the coaction of $D$ but not under the coaction of $C$, a contradiction. Thus $f$ has to be pure.
nodes.statement_short: If $f$ were not pure, the kernel modulo some ideal $I$ would be $D$-stable but not $C$-stable.

nodes.name: Converse of (2) via the purity intersection identity
nodes.statement: For the converse, assuming that $f:C\to D$ is injective and pure and $N\subset M$ be $R$-modules, then we have the equality of submodules of $M\otimes D$: $$N\otimes D\cap M\otimes C=N\otimes C,$$ where $C$ is considered as an $R$-submodule of $D$ by means of $f$. Hence, if $M$ is a $C$-comodule and $N$ is a $D$-subcomodule of $M$, then, denote by $\delta$ the coaction, we have $$\delta(N)\subset N\otimes D\cap M\otimes C=N\otimes C.$$ That is, $N$ is stable under the coaction of $C$.
nodes.statement_short: Purity gives $N\otimes D\cap M\otimes C=N\otimes C$, so $\delta(N)\subset N\otimes C$.

nodes.name: Torsion part as the kernel of localization
nodes.statement: $$M^\text{tor}={\rm ker}(M\to M\otimes K).$$

nodes.name: Torsion commutes with tensoring by a flat module
nodes.statement: $$(M^\text{tor}\otimes P)\cong (M\otimes P)^\text{tor}.$$

nodes.name: Intersection identity for a pure inclusion $C\subset D$
nodes.statement: $$N\otimes D\cap M\otimes C=N\otimes C,$$

nodes.statement: Since $D$ is projective, the natural functor ${\rm comod}(D)\to \mod(D^\vee)$ is fully faithful, exact with image closed under taking subobjects \cite[3.10]{Ha}.
nodes.statement_short: For projective $D$, $\comod(D)\to\mod(D^\vee)$ is fully faithful, exact and subobject-closed.

conclusions: the natural functor ${\rm comod}(D)\to \mod(D^\vee)$ is fully faithful, exact with image closed under taking subobjects

nodes.statement: According to Serre \cite[Prop.~2]{Se}, any object in $\comod(C)$ is the union of its $R$-finite subcomodules (but generally not saturated). I don't know if one can prove Propsition \ref{prop9b} with $\comod(C)$, $\comod(D)$ replaced by $\comod_f(C)$, $\comod_f(D)$, respectively.

nodes.name: Serre, Prop. 2 (comodules are unions of $R$-finite subcomodules)
nodes.statement: According to Serre \cite[Prop.~2]{Se}, any object in $\comod(C)$ is the union of its $R$-finite subcomodules (but generally not saturated).
conclusions: any object in $\comod(C)$ is the union of its $R$-finite subcomodules (but generally not saturated)
